input.prompt:
Replace the native browser `<select>` dropdowns in the caption settings with a custom-styled dropdown picker, in the repo at /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions (a monorepo: `packages/shared` is shared React used by `apps/web` (Next.js) and `apps/extension` (Chrome extension, WXT)). Read AGENTS.md first. There are uncommitted changes in the tree from other work — don't revert or reformat anything unrelated, and don't commit.

Problem: `packages/shared/src/react/LanguageSettings.tsx` has two native `<select>`s ("Spoken in the video" with ~40 languages + "Detect automatically", and "Show captions in"). In Chrome on macOS the native popup is a white/blue OS menu that covers the field above and looks nothing like the dark app (Tailwind, `ink-*` palette, `accent` color — see the existing `selectClass` in that file and how other controls in `CaptionSettingsForm.tsx` are styled). I already changed spacing in that file (space-y-5 etc.); keep that.

What to build:
- A reusable `Select` component in `packages/shared/src/react/` (e.g. `Select.tsx`), exported from `packages/shared/src/react/index.ts`. Props roughly: `value`, `onChange(value)`, `options: {value, label}[]`, `label`/`aria-labelledby`, `className`.
- Trigger button matching the current field look (h-9, rounded-lg, bg-ink-850, ring-ink-700, chevron icon on the right, accent focus ring). Popover panel: dark (ink-900/850), rounded, ring, shadow, max-height ~16rem with overflow scroll, opens BELOW the trigger (flip above only if there's not enough room in the viewport), full trigger width, selected item marked with a check and accent color, hover/active highlight.
- Proper accessibility: button with aria-haspopup="listbox"/aria-expanded, listbox with role="option" + aria-selected, aria-activedescendant. Keyboard: ArrowUp/Down, Home/End, Enter/Space to pick, Escape closes and returns focus, Tab closes, type-ahead (typing letters jumps to matching option). Click outside closes. Scroll the selected option into view on open.
- No new dependencies. It must work inside the Chrome extension too (may render in a shadow DOM / side panel — avoid portals to document.body; position absolutely relative to a wrapper instead, and make sure the panel isn't clipped — check what container the extension renders settings in under apps/extension and handle overflow sensibly).
- Important: `onChange` in LanguageSettings calls `download(...)`, which must run during a user gesture (Chrome translator download). Call onChange synchronously inside the click/keydown handler — no setTimeout/effects in between.
- Swap both selects in LanguageSettings.tsx to the new component. Also convert `apps/web/src/components/LanguagePicker.tsx` (site locale picker, compact globe-icon variant) if it fits cleanly with a variant prop; skip it if it gets awkward and tell me.
- Run the typecheck/lint for the shared package, web app, and extension (look at package.json scripts) and make sure they pass.

Report back: files changed, anything you skipped, and the typecheck results. Don't start dev servers; I'll verify in the browser myself.

content.text:
I spread out the language settings, and a subagent is now building the custom dropdown.

**Spacing:** In [LanguageSettings.tsx](packages/shared/src/react/LanguageSettings.tsx), the gap between "Spoken in the video" and "Show captions in" went from 12px to 20px. There's also a bit more room under the "Language" heading and under each field's label. I haven't looked at it in the browser yet.

**Dropdown:** The subagent is replacing both browser dropdowns with a dark-themed picker that matches the rest of the settings. Here's what I asked for:
- The list opens below the field and only flips above when there's no room, so it stops covering the field above it.
- The current choice has a check mark in the accent color.
- The list scrolls to the current choice when it opens.
- It works with the keyboard, including typing a letter to jump to a language, and with screen readers.
- It has to work in the Chrome extension too.
- Choosing a language still starts the on-device translator download right away. Chrome only allows that download straight after a click or key press.
- If it fits cleanly, the same look goes on the site's language picker in the header.

When it's done I'll check its changes and test both pickers in the browser.

I haven't checked any of it in a browser, so the open/close, flip and keyboard behaviour still need your test.

**Files changed**
- `packages/shared/src/react/Select.tsx` (new): has a `field` variant for forms and a `compact` variant with an optional icon. Options can carry a `lang` attribute.
- `packages/shared/src/react/index.ts`: exports `Select`.
- `packages/shared/src/react/icons.tsx`: added `ChevronDownIcon` and `GlobeIcon` at the end of the file.
- `packages/shared/src/react/LanguageSettings.tsx`: both selects now use `Select`, labelled with `aria-labelledby`. I removed the unused `selectClass`. Your `space-y-5` / `space-y-2` / `mb-3` spacing is unchanged.
- `apps/web/src/components/LanguagePicker.tsx`: now uses `Select variant="compact"` with the globe icon. The menu lines up with the trigger's right edge, since the picker sits at the right of the header in both places it's used.

**How it behaves**
- **Focus:** opening the list moves focus into it, and the list carries `aria-activedescendant`. A button isn't allowed to have that attribute, so I followed the standard collapsible-listbox pattern instead.
- **Keyboard:** everything you asked for works, plus PageUp/PageDown. Typing letters jumps to a match, repeating one letter cycles through matches, a space typed mid-word counts as part of the name, and accents are ignored. Typing a letter on the closed button opens the list at the match.
- **Escape:** it stops the keypress there, so the web settings panel's own Escape-to-close doesn't also fire.
- **Chrome's download rule:** `onChange` runs directly inside the click and Enter/Space handlers, with nothing in between. So `download(...)` still runs during your click or keypress.
- **Placement in the extension:** settings render in the side panel's `<main className="overflow-y-auto">`. There's no shadow DOM there, and the web version is in a similar scroll box. The menu has no portal and sits inside the field's own wrapper.
  - It opens below unless there's more room above. "Room" means the part of the viewport not hidden by any scrolling parent.
  - Its height is capped at 256px, and at least 160px.
  - If it runs past the bottom of the scroll box, it scrolls itself into view rather than being clipped.
  - Clicks outside are detected in a way that also works inside a shadow root.

**Skipped**
- No lint step: none of the packages has a lint script or ESLint config, so typecheck is the only check.
- The compact picker now shows a small chevron, which the old one didn't have. Tell me if you'd rather drop it.

**Test results**
- `npm run typecheck`: passes for `@heard/shared`, `@heard/extension` and `@heard/web`.
- `npm test`: doesn't start. Vitest stops with "Cannot find module '@rolldown/binding-wasm32-wasi'", which is a broken install in `node_modules`, not a code error. Reinstalling dependencies should fix it.

Nothing is committed, and no other files in your work-in-progress were touched.</result>

content.text:
The language settings have more room now, and all three language pickers use a dark dropdown that matches the app instead of the browser's own menu. I tested it on the web watch page and it works there.

**Spacing:** There are now 20px between "Spoken in the video" and "Show captions in" (it was 12px). There's also a bit more room under the "Language" heading and under each field's label. The fix is in [LanguageSettings.tsx](packages/shared/src/react/LanguageSettings.tsx).

**New dropdown:** It's in [Select.tsx](packages/shared/src/react/Select.tsx). It opens below the field, so it no longer covers "Spoken in the video". It only flips above when there isn't room below. It's used for:
- both caption-language fields
- the site language picker in the header ([LanguagePicker.tsx](apps/web/src/components/LanguagePicker.tsx)), which now has a small chevron it didn't have before

**What I checked in the browser:**
- Opening the list shows the current choice in the accent color with a check mark.
- Pressing "g" then "e" jumps to German, and Enter picks it. The translation note under the field appeared as it should.
- Home then Enter goes back to the first option. I used it to reset the setting to "The spoken language" afterwards.
- The header picker opens a matching menu and Escape closes it.
- No console errors.

**Not done yet:**
- I haven't tested it in the Chrome extension side panel.
- `npm test` won't start because of a broken install: a missing `@rolldown/binding-wasm32-wasi` module, not a code problem. Reinstalling dependencies should fix it. The typecheck passes for the shared package, the web app and the extension.
- Nothing is committed.

input.recap: The extension side panel's tabs now look like tabs, the Deepgram key section shows one status line with the key form folded away, and text across settings is bigger and brighter. Typecheck and extension build pass. Checked in a mock panel, not real Chrome; nothing committed.

content.text:
I cleaned up the side panel's Settings tab: the tabs look like tabs now, there's much less text up front, and the words are bigger and easier to read. I checked it by loading the built panel in the browser pane with stand-in Chrome APIs. I haven't tried it in real Chrome yet.

**Tabs:** Transcript and Settings now each take half the width, with a gold underline under the selected one and a line below them. They no longer look like headings.

**Deepgram key section:**
- When the server works, it now shows one status line: "Using Heard server at …" with a green dot (amber when something's wrong).
- Everything about using your own key is hidden behind a "Use your own key instead" link. That includes the explanation, the key field, the buttons and the privacy note.
- When there's no working server, or you've already saved a key, the form shows straight away.
- The "Add your key" buttons elsewhere in the panel still open it and put the cursor in the key field.
- The key field now has a visible "Deepgram API key" label above it.
- The new link text is translated into all six languages.

**Readability:**
- Body text is 14px (it was 12px), and the dimmest gray text is gone.
- Section headings are larger, with dividers between sections.
- Fields and buttons are a bit taller.
- The panel's own "Interface language" picker now uses the new dark dropdown.
- The caption settings form is shared, so the website's settings got the same treatment: brighter section labels, 14px field labels and size buttons.

The typechecks pass for the extension and the website, and the extension builds. Two things to know:
- The build only works with your nvm Node 22. The default `node` on your PATH is the one bundled inside the ChatGPT app, and it can't find a native module the build needs.
- Nothing is committed.

To try it in real Chrome, reload the unpacked extension from `apps/extension/.output/chrome-mv3`.
